spark.summary: CI/CD quality gates are automated, deterministic checkpoints—spanning unit/contract tests, SAST/SCA security scans, policy-as-code, and canary SLO analysis—that block defective or vulnerable artifacts from advancing toward production.

spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** **CI/CD quality gates** are automated, non-negotiable verification checkpoints placed along the path from `git push` to 100% production traffic.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts PR Fast Gate (<3m) -> Merge Queue (5-10m) -> Policy Gate -> Canary SLO (PR Gate (<3m) -> Merge Queue (8m) -> OPA / Kyverno -> Canary SLO Gate); CI Test Health & Quarantine State Machine (BLOCKING GATE -> QUARANTINED -> SLA REPAIRED); PR -> Merge Queue -> Cosign Attestation -> Kyverno -> Canary (PR / Dev -> Merge Queue -> OCI + Cosign -> K8s + Argo).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Replace brittle, slow end-to-end staging suites with fast consumer-driven contracts and production canary analysis. In a high-velocity platform, PRs clear fast static/unit gates in `<3m`, enter a **speculative Merge Queue** for Pact + Testcontainers + Trivy + Cosign signing, and deploy via Argo.

**Failure Modes & Application:** Connect quality gates to canary rollbacks, contract testing, and flake reduction.

learningJourney.title: What are CI/CD Quality Gates
learningJourney.explanation:
**CI/CD quality gates** are automated, non-negotiable verification checkpoints placed along the path from `git push` to 100% production traffic. Instead of relying on manual QA sign-offs, gates encode engineering, security, and reliability standards into executable checks.

The core design principle is **tiered latency matching** (the Testing Trophy): fast deterministic checks (`gitleaks`, `semgrep` SAST, `buf breaking`, unit tests) fail bad PRs in `<3 minutes`; Pact contract tests, Testcontainers, Trivy CVE scans, and **Cosign** signing run in the merge queue (`5–10m`); and **Canary SLO gates** verify live p99 and 5xx in production.

sectionDiagram.title: PR Fast Gate (<3m) -> Merge Queue (5-10m) -> Policy Gate -> Canary SLO

cards.label: Fast-Fail Feedback
cards.detail: Developers get deterministic unit/SAST feedback in <3 minutes without waiting on 30-minute E2E suites.

cards.label: Policy-as-Code
cards.detail: OPA/Conftest and Kyverno block public S3 buckets, missing resource limits, and :latest tags.

cards.label: SLSA Provenance
cards.detail: Keyless Cosign signatures bind the built digest to its exact CI workflow and commit SHA.

sectionDiagram.summary: Tiered quality gates match check latency to pipeline stage so velocity and safety reinforce each other.

learningJourney.title: Why we need Tiered Gates (and how flaky/slow gates fail)
learningJourney.explanation:
Badly designed CI gates hurt both reliability and velocity:

1. **Flaky Test Erosion**: A 5% flaky integration test trains developers to hit 'Re-run' blindly, masking real regressions.
2. **Slow-Gate Queue Jamming**: Putting a 35-minute E2E suite as a blocking PR check creates a 10-PR backlog and forces teams to bundle risky giant diffs.
3. **Canary Blind Spots**: Checking only HTTP `5xx` in a canary gate misses silent latency regressions (`p99` doubling) or business conversion drops.

sectionDiagram.title: CI Test Health & Quarantine State Machine
sectionDiagram.summary: Auto-quarantining flaky tests preserves developer trust in blocking gates while tracking repair SLAs.

ideas.title: Track DORA Metrics
ideas.description: Target Change Failure Rate (CFR) < 5% and Stage 1 PR feedback < 5 minutes; feed escaped incidents back into new contract/canary checks.

ideas.title: Zero Unaudited Bypasses
ideas.description: Never allow silent --no-verify or admin merge overrides without an audited reason and post-merge tracking.

learningJourney.purpose: The problem: see what breaks without Tiered Gates under real concurrency or scale.

learningJourney.title: Where Quality Gates apply across the SDLC
learningJourney.explanation: Place each check at the earliest stage where it can run fast and deterministically.

benefits: Catches secrets (gitleaks), SAST (semgrep), Protobuf breaking changes (buf), and unit logic immediately.
costs: Cannot catch real Postgres/Kafka integration bugs or multi-service contract drift.

benefits: Runs Testcontainers, Pact consumer contracts, Trivy CVE scans, and Cosign signing on serialized merges.
costs: Requires merge-queue batching/speculative checks under high commit volume.

benefits: Kyverno blocks unsigned/:latest pods; Argo AnalysisTemplate aborts bad canaries on real golden signals.
costs: Requires Prometheus/SLO instrumentation and rollback automation.

learningJourney.title: How GitHub Actions Gates & OPA/Conftest Policies are written
learningJourney.explanation: Run fast PR checks in parallel, enforce policy-as-code on Terraform/Kubernetes manifests, and sign every promoted digest.
learningJourney.markdownContent:
```yaml
# Fast-to-slow GitHub Actions PR quality gate workflow
name: pr-quality-gates
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  fast-static-and-unit:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Secret & SAST Scan
        run: |
          gitleaks detect --no-git --redact
          semgrep --config p/owasp-top-ten --error
      - name: Policy-as-Code (Conftest / OPA)
        run: conftest test deploy/k8s/*.yaml -p policy/
      - name: Unit Tests & Diff Coverage
        run: pytest --cov=app --cov-fail-under=80
```

benefits: Verifies API schemas and real DB/Kafka behavior in <5 minutes per service independently.
costs: Requires teams to publish and version Pact contracts in a broker.

benefits: Catches real-world load, memory, and latency regressions safely on 1-5% traffic.
costs: Must have automated rollback and sufficient traffic sample size.

knowledgeCheck.question: Your team's PR pipeline runs a 35-minute full-stack E2E suite on every commit, causing developers to batch huge PRs and blindly re-run flaky failures. How should you restructure the gates?

options.text: Keep PR gates <3m (unit, SAST, lint), move Pact contracts/Testcontainers to the merge queue, and quarantine flaky tests with a repair SLA
options.feedback: Correct: tiered latency matching restores fast PR feedback while preserving strong integration and runtime canary safety.

options.text: Delete all automated tests and rely on manual QA
options.feedback: Manual QA slows releases further and misses regressions.

options.text: Allow developers to merge with failing checks
options.feedback: Bypassing broken gates destroys pipeline signal.

_recommendedProblem.title: Active-Active Multi-Master Split-Brain Recovery
_recommendedProblem.prompt: Redesign an active-active multi-master relational replication pipeline between us-east-1 and eu-west-1 (6,000 writes/sec, 85 ms WAN RTT, < 15 ms p99 local commit) so a 9-minute transatlantic partition and 180-250 ms NTP clock skew never cause silent Last-Write-Wins (LWW) overwrites.
